raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Before submitting

- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply, or I explain the exception below.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

## Affected area

FE OSS kernels or CuTeDSL

- `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm120/epilogue_codegen.py` (`_tap_fake_shape`)
- tests: `test/python/gemm/frost/test_matmul.py`, `test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py`, `test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py`

## Summary

The SM120 FROST GEMM codegen now declares the compile-time fake of a non-segmented quant-scale output (the scale tensor of `block_scale_quantize`) with a fresh `cute.sym_int64()` for every non-unit extent.

Before, `_tap_fake_shape` emitted the kernel's own `sym_m` for the scale's rows whenever they equalled the kernel's build M, and a literal otherwise. It treated the other two extents the same way with `(sym_n // block_size)` and `sym_l`, but those never refused a call: TVM-FFI binds the derived `(sym_n // block_size)` to a Var of its own, and the dense batch is fixed. Only the `sym_m` binding was a real tie.

Nothing else changes. The epilogue stores the scales through the tap's raw pointer with the same index math, and the host checks of the scale buffer are untouched.

## Why

The scale buffer of a `block_scale_quantize` output is a plan constant. Its output rule is CONST (`recipe._output_rule`), and on SM120 `_check_runtime_quant` re-runs the quant gates at the call's kernel-frame (M, N). A call that keeps the padded extents is therefore admitted. An F8_128x4 row-quant scale has rup(M, 128) rows, so a plan built at M = 256 admits a call at M = 200 with the same [1, 256, 8] scale buffer.

The compile fake disagreed with that contract. The kernel's M is the graph's M (the token count S for MoE), or the graph's N in a swap-AB plan, which runs the graph transposed. `_tap_fake_shape` emitted `sym_m` for the scale's rows whenever they equalled that M at build time. For example:

- row quant: whenever M (S) is a multiple of 128;
- col quant: whenever rup(N, 128) == M;
- swap-AB row quant: whenever rup(M, 128) == N (rup(S, 128) == N for MoE).

The TVM-FFI spec converter allocates one Var per `SymInt` object, so every launch then checked the scale's row count against the kernel's runtime M.

Minimal reproducer on an RTX PRO 6000 (SM120):

- Graph: bf16 A [1, 256, 128] (K-major) times bf16 B [1, 128, 256], then `matmul`, then `block_scale_quantize(block_size=32, axis=-1)`. The data output is FP8_E4M3 [1, 256, 256]; the scale is FP8_E8M0 [1, 256, 8] with `F8_128x4` reordering.
- Call: build the FROST plan, then run it with A [1, 200, 128], data output [1, 200, 256] and the same [1, 256, 8] scale buffer.
- Observed: `ValueError: Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0] on argument #4 when calling: _host(...), expected to match a_0.shape[0]`. The error is the same through `graph.execute(...)` with the M = 200 buffers, through `graph.execute_plan_at_index(...)` with `override_shapes`, and through the plan from `jit_from_cudnn_graph`.
- Expected: the call runs, as FROST's own checks allow. A plan of the same graph built at an unaligned M (for example 200, whose fake carries the literal 256) runs every M in that padding.

The other affected plans fail the same way:

- The plain MoE template `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py` and the block-scaled MoE template `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py`, where `sym_m` is the token count S. They refuse S = 200 after a build at S = 256 (on argument #6 and #8).
- Swap-AB plans, on another axis. In dense swap-AB (`sm120_matmul.py` on the transposed chain), `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py` and `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py`, `sym_m` is the graph's N (the weight-feature extent). The fake therefore tied the scale rows rup(M, 128) to N when the two were equal. Token-count changes kept working, but a call that changed N inside the scale padding was refused:
  - dense swap-AB built at M = N = 256 and called with N = 224: `Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0] on argument #4`;
  - MoE swap-AB and block-scaled MoE swap-AB built at S = N = 256 and called at S = 200 with weights of N = 224: the same error on #6 and #8.
- GATHER plans, plain and block-scaled, render the same fake. A GATHER plan counts S in routed rows (the `token_index` extent), and the token operand's source rows have a symbol of their own (`sym_source_m`, or `sym_source_n` in the swap-AB templates). So `sym_m` is the routed S in the normal orientation and the weights' N under swap-AB, and the scale rows were tied the same way. Built at 256 routed rows gathered from 137 token rows:
  - plain and block-scaled (NVFP4) GATHER plans refuse a call at 200 routed rows, on argument #7 and #9;
  - their swap-AB versions refuse a call at 200 routed rows with weights of N = 224, on the same arguments. As in the other swap-AB plans, a call that changes only the routed rows runs.

Not affected: segmented (per-group) scales already used fresh symbols. COMBINE plans allow no operation after the grouped GEMM, so they cannot carry a quant-scale output. SCATTER plans cannot either: `_check_executable` declines a SCATTER graph with quantization or a reduction (`sm120/compiler.py:1608-1610`). `sm120_block_scale_matmul.py` declines quant epilogues on SM120 (`_DENSE_BLOCK_SCALE_QUANT_DECLINE`).

Why this fix:

- The fake only gives TVM-FFI its calling convention. The epilogue addresses the scale blob through `mC_tap_i.iterator.raw_ptr()`, with plan-literal and `problem_size` stride math.
- The host already holds the buffer to the declared shape: the CONST output check in `lowered()` on the dense path, and `_expected_output_shape` in every MoE launcher, including the swap-AB one. It also holds the buffer to the runtime padding through `_check_runtime_quant`, which runs on every SM120 path: all three SM120 compiled classes set `_validate_runtime_quant`, and `_launch_moe_swap_ab` calls it directly.
- Fresh symbols match two existing patterns: the segmented-scale branch directly above in the same function, and the SFA / SFB fakes of the block-scale templates.

The audit named one other option: emit the declared extents as literals. I did not take it. Literals would put the padded M bucket into the rendered source. Dense row-quant plans built at M = 256 and M = 384 render one source today and share one compiled artifact; with literals they would compile separately, which is the over-keying that Rule 4 warns against. With fresh symbols, these builds render byte-identical sources:

- dense row-quant plans built at M = 200, 256 and 384
- MoE plans built at S = 200, 256 and 384

This was found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding B33).

## Related issues

None. Related to these open PRs of the same audit series, which also change the F8_128x4 quant-scale output path:

- #2011 (B03) zeroes the K padding of F8_128x4 quant-scale rows, in the block-quant emitters of the same `sm120/epilogue_codegen.py`.
- #2033 (B28) computes the col-quant F8_128x4 scale offset in Int64, in `_emit_block_quant_col` of the same file.
- #2017 (B27) refuses F8_128x4 quant-scale buffers whose batch planes are not packed byte runs, next to the host checks this PR relies on (`compiler.py`, `sm120/compiler.py`).

#2011 and #2017 also add tests to the same three test files. #2013 (B14) and #2031 (B15) edit other functions (the reduction emitters) of `sm120/epilogue_codegen.py`. Trial merges (`git merge-tree`) of this branch with the current heads of the other branches of the series are textually clean.

## API and compatibility impact

- Some calls passed FROST's own checks but were refused by the TVM-FFI front door. They now run. These are calls on plans whose non-segmented quant-scale rows equalled the kernel's build M, where the call moves the kernel's M but keeps the F8_128x4 padded extents. For example:
  - a runtime M (dense) or S (MoE; routed rows for GATHER) that differs from the build value, on plans with a row-quant scale built at a 128-aligned M (S), or with a col-quant scale where rup(N, 128) == M;
  - in swap-AB plans (dense, MoE and block-scaled MoE, including GATHER), a runtime N that differs from the build value, on plans whose row-quant scale rows rup(M, 128) (rup(S, 128) for MoE) equal the build N.

  No graph is newly declined, and the numerics of calls that ran before are unchanged.
- Calls that change the padded extents are still refused before launch with the same `scale_dim` ValueError (`F8_128x4 ... block_scale_quantize scale output currently requires scale_dim=...`). On the dense path it comes through `explain()`, which adds its existing kernel-frame note for swap-AB plans; the MoE launchers raise it directly from `_check_runtime_quant`. The new dense test checks this for each of its cases.
- The rendered kernel source changes for plans with a non-segmented quant-scale output, so their cached kernels recompile once.
- SM100: the same code is at `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:440` (`_tap_fake_shape`, lines 423-443). It is intentionally left for a follow-up; the repo convention is that such fixes land in both trees. Two notes for that follow-up, both from reading the code only (no SM100 GPU was available, so neither was run):
  - The SM100 compiled classes do not set `_validate_runtime_quant`, so the SM100 dense and non-swap MoE launches do not re-check the quant extents at runtime (the SM100 MoE swap-AB launcher does, inline). On those two paths, for 128-aligned builds, the `sym_m` tie is what currently refuses a runtime M whose padded rows exceed the declared blob. Porting this change alone would remove that refusal, so the port also needs the host-side runtime quant check there.
  - An SM100 dense or non-swap MoE plan built at an unaligned M already renders a literal scale extent, and I found no other runtime check that holds a call to that plan's padding. Such a plan may therefore already admit a runtime M whose padded rows exceed the declared blob, and store past it.

## Testing

Environment: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All commands ran from `test/python`.

New tests (ten cases):

- `test_matmul.py::test_sm120_quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime_m_in_its_padding`, with four cases:
  - `row`: built at M = 256, called at M = 200.
  - `row_unaligned_build`: built at M = 200, called at M = 256. This is a control that passes on base too.
  - `col_square`: built at M = N = 256, called at M = 224.
  - `row_swap_ab`: a swap-AB plan built at M = N = 256, called with N = 224.

  Each case checks the data and the scale bytes exactly against a torch reference. It then checks that a call with 128 more rows is refused with the `scale_dim` message. That probe's scale buffer keeps the declared shape and strides, but it is a view into storage sized for the probe's own padded extents, so a regressed host check could not write past the allocation.
- `test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py::test_moe_quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime_s_in_its_padding_sm120`, with four cases:
  - `normal` and `swap_ab`: built at S = N = 256 and called at S = 200; the `swap_ab` case is also called with weights of N = 224.
  - `gather` and `gather_swap_ab`: the same with GATHER plans, built at 256 routed rows gathered from 137 token rows and called at 200 routed rows. `_build_graph` takes a `gather_rows` argument for this, like the block-scaled helper.
- `test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py::test_e2e_quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime_s_in_its_padding_sm120`, cases `normal` and `swap_ab`: the same as the first two MoE cases, with NVFP4 operands.

Each test also asserts that the plan has the intended `swap_ab` setting, and the plain MoE test asserts the plan's MoE mode (`none` or `gather`).

RED on base, GREEN on this branch. For base, the new test files were copied into a detached worktree of 24a8cd43:

```
python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_matmul.py gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py -k quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime
```

- base 24a8cd43: `9 failed, 1 passed, 8470 deselected`. Each failure is `ValueError: Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0]`: on argument #4 for the three dense cases (`row`, `col_square`, `row_swap_ab`), #6 for the MoE `normal` and `swap_ab` cases, #7 for the two GATHER cases and #8 for both block-scaled MoE cases. Each failure says `expected to match a_0.shape[0]`, except the `gather` case, which says `expected to match token_index.shape[0]`: in that plan the first argument bound to `sym_m` is `token_index`, whose length is the routed S. The pass is the `row_unaligned_build` control.
- branch: `10 passed, 8470 deselected`.

Related existing tests:

- `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k sm120`
  - base: `1 failed, 1036 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected`
  - branch: `1 failed, 1046 passed, 82 skipped, 9789 deselected`

  The difference is the ten new test cases. The one failure is present on base: `test_matmul.py::test_sm120_epi_vec_clamp_and_stg_only`, which asserts the SM100 TMA-store choice through the facade in an SM120 process.
- `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost -k "quant and not sm120"`: `5 failed, 41 passed, 193 skipped, 10679 deselected` on both base (with the new test files copied in) and branch. The failures are the same `test_tile_select_analytic.py` planner tests on both.
- `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -p no:xdist gemm/frost/test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py`, for the `_build_graph` change:
  - base: `2 failed, 124 passed, 395 skipped`
  - branch: `2 failed, 128 passed, 395 skipped`

  The difference is the four new MoE cases. Both failures are present on base: `test_moe_tma_store_uses_rank2_output_descriptor[n]` and `[m]` fail with an `ImportError` (`_host_tma_c_descs` from the SM120 compiler) in an SM120 process.
- Engine-path files with quant outputs, with `-k "not sm120"`: `46 passed, 184 skipped, 3 deselected` on both base and branch. The files are `test_flashinfer_shaped_gemm.py`, `test_stream_respect.py`, `test_public_execute_flavors.py`, `test_execute_recipe.py`, `test_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_epilogue_fusion.py`, `test_block_scale_matmul_swiglu.py`, `test_matmul_swiglu.py` and `test_gemm_python_validate.py`.
- `pre-commit run --files` on the four changed files: black, black-jupyter and the SPDX header check passed.

Ad-hoc checks, not committed:

- On the M = 256 dense plan, the public graph path fails with the ValueError on base and runs on this branch. This covers both `graph.execute` with M = 200 buffers and `execute_plan_at_index` with `override_shapes`.
- Block-scaled NVFP4 GATHER plans (K = 256), normal and swap-AB, with the same build and calls as the two GATHER test cases: base renders the scale fake as `(sym_m, (sym_n // 32), 1)` and refuses the calls with `Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0] on argument #9`. This branch renders `(cute.sym_int64(), cute.sym_int64(), 1)` and runs them with exact data and scales.
- A SCATTER graph with a `block_scale_quantize` output: `jit_from_cudnn_graph` of the SM120 compiler declines it with `NotImplementedError: MoE SCATTER currently supports dense pointwise outputs without quantization or reduction`, normal and swap-AB, on base and on this branch.

Not tested:

- SM10.x: all ten new test cases skip there, so they need an SM120 GPU to run. The dense and plain MoE tests plan an SM120 config through the facade `_plan`, which the sm100 tree declines (the frost conftest reports that as a skip), and the block-scaled MoE test is marked `requires_sm120`.
- SM100 itself: no SM100 GPU was available, and the sm100 tree is unchanged.

- Call: build the FROST plan, then run it with A [1, 200, 128], data output [1, 200, 256] and the same [1, 256, 8] scale buffer.
- Observed: `ValueError: Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0] on argument #4 when calling: _host(...), expected to match a_0.shape[0]`. The error is the same through `graph.execute(...)` with the M = 200 buffers, through `graph.execute_plan_at_index(...)` with `override_shapes`, and through the plan from `jit_from_cudnn_graph`.
- Expected: the call runs, as FROST's own checks allow. A plan of the same graph built at an unaligned M (for example 200, whose fake carries the literal 256) runs every M in that padding.

The other affected plans fail the same way:

- The plain MoE template `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd.py` and the block-scaled MoE template `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd.py`, where `sym_m` is the token count S. They refuse S = 200 after a build at S = 256 (on argument #6 and #8).
- Swap-AB plans, on another axis. In dense swap-AB (`sm120_matmul.py` on the transposed chain), `sm120_moe_grouped_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py` and `sm120_moe_grouped_block_scale_matmul_fwd_swap_ab.py`, `sym_m` is the graph's N (the weight-feature extent). The fake therefore tied the scale rows rup(M, 128) to N when the two were equal. Token-count changes kept working, but a call that changed N inside the scale padding was refused:
  - dense swap-AB built at M = N = 256 and called with N = 224: `Mismatched c_tap_1.shape[0] on argument #4`;
  - MoE swap-AB and block-scaled MoE swap-AB built at S = N = 256 and called at S = 200 with weights of N = 224: the same error on #6 and #8.
- GATHER plans, plain and block-scaled, render the same fake. A GATHER plan counts S in routed rows (the `token_index` extent), and the token operand's source rows have a symbol of their own (`sym_source_m`, or `sym_source_n` in the swap-AB templates). So `sym_m` is the routed S in the normal orientation and the weights' N under swap-AB, and the scale rows were tied the same way. Built at 256 routed rows gathered from 137 token rows:
  - plain and block-scaled (NVFP4) GATHER plans refuse a call at 200 routed rows, on argument #7 and #9;
  - their swap-AB versions refuse a call at 200 routed rows with weights of N = 224, on the same arguments. As in the other swap-AB plans, a call that changes only the routed rows runs.

Not affected: segmented (per-group) scales already used fresh symbols. COMBINE plans allow no operation after the grouped GEMM, so they cannot carry a quant-scale output. SCATTER plans cannot either: `_check_executable` declines a SCATTER graph with quantization or a reduction (`sm120/compiler.py:1608-1610`). `sm120_block_scale_matmul.py` declines quant epilogues on SM120 (`_DENSE_BLOCK_SCALE_QUANT_DECLINE`).

Why this fix:

- The fake only gives TVM-FFI its calling convention. The epilogue addresses the scale blob through `mC_tap_i.iterator.raw_ptr()`, with plan-literal and `problem_size` stride math.
- The host already holds the buffer to the declared shape: the CONST output check in `lowered()` on the dense path, and `_expected_output_shape` in every MoE launcher, including the swap-AB one. It also holds the buffer to the runtime padding through `_check_runtime_quant`, which runs on every SM120 path: all three SM120 compiled classes set `_validate_runtime_quant`, and `_launch_moe_swap_ab` calls it directly.
- Fresh symbols match two existing patterns: the segmented-scale branch directly above in the same function, and the SFA / SFB fakes of the block-scale templates.

The audit named one other option: emit the declared extents as literals. I did not take it. Literals would put the padded M bucket into the rendered source. Dense row-quant plans built at M = 256 and M = 384 render one source today and share one compiled artifact; with literals they would compile separately, which is the over-keying that Rule 4 warns against. With fresh symbols, these builds render byte-identical sources:

- dense row-quant plans built at M = 200, 256 and 384
- MoE plans built at S = 200, 256 and 384

This was found in an audit of the SM120 Frost kernel templates (finding B33).

## Related issues

None. Related to these open PRs of the same audit series, which also change the F8_128x4 quant-scale output path:

- #2011 (B03) zeroes the K padding of F8_128x4 quant-scale rows, in the block-quant emitters of the same `sm120/epilogue_codegen.py`.
- #2033 (B28) computes the col-quant F8_128x4 scale offset in Int64, in `_emit_block_quant_col` of the same file.
- #2017 (B27) refuses F8_128x4 quant-scale buffers whose batch planes are not packed byte runs, next to the host checks this PR relies on (`compiler.py`, `sm120/compiler.py`).

#2011 and #2017 also add tests to the same three test files. #2013 (B14) and #2031 (B15) edit other functions (the reduction emitters) of `sm120/epilogue_codegen.py`. Trial merges (`git merge-tree`) of this branch with the current heads of the other branches of the series are textually clean.

## API and compatibility impact

- Some calls passed FROST's own checks but were refused by the TVM-FFI front door. They now run. These are calls on plans whose non-segmented quant-scale rows equalled the kernel's build M, where the call moves the kernel's M but keeps the F8_128x4 padded extents. For example:
  - a runtime M (dense) or S (MoE; routed rows for GATHER) that differs from the build value, on plans with a row-quant scale built at a 128-aligned M (S), or with a col-quant scale where rup(N, 128) == M;
  - in swap-AB plans (dense, MoE and block-scaled MoE, including GATHER), a runtime N that differs from the build value, on plans whose row-quant scale rows rup(M, 128) (rup(S, 128) for MoE) equal the build N.

  No graph is newly declined, and the numerics of calls that ran before are unchanged.
- Calls that change the padded extents are still refused before launch with the same `scale_dim` ValueError (`F8_128x4 ... block_scale_quantize scale output currently requires scale_dim=...`). On the dense path it comes through `explain()`, which adds its existing kernel-frame note for swap-AB plans; the MoE launchers raise it directly from `_check_runtime_quant`. The new dense test checks this for each of its cases.
- The rendered kernel source changes for plans with a non-segmented quant-scale output, so their cached kernels recompile once.
- SM100: the same code is at `python/cudnn/gemm/frost/sm100/epilogue_codegen.py:440` (`_tap_fake_shape`, lines 423-443). It is intentionally left for a follow-up; the repo convention is that such fixes land in both trees. Two notes for that follow-up, both from reading the code only (no SM100 GPU was available, so neither was run):
  - The SM100 compiled classes do not set `_validate_runtime_quant`, so the SM100 dense and non-swap MoE launches do not re-check the quant extents at runtime (the SM100 MoE swap-AB launcher does, inline). On those two paths, for 128-aligned builds, the `sym_m` tie is what currently refuses a runtime M whose padded rows exceed the declared blob. Porting this change alone would remove that refusal, so the port also needs the host-side runtime quant check there.
  - An SM100 dense or non-swap MoE plan built at an unaligned M already renders a literal scale extent, and I found no other runtime check that holds a call to that plan's padding. Such a plan may therefore already admit a runtime M whose padded rows exceed the declared blob, and store past it.

## Testing

Environment: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (SM120), CUDA 13.4, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.7.1, torch 2.14.0+cu130, cuDNN 9.24, frontend bindings built from develop 24a8cd43. All commands ran from `test/python`.

+def test_moe_quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime_s_in_its_padding_sm120(gather, swap_ab, call_n):
+    """MoE twin of test_matmul.py::test_sm120_quant_scale_blob_admits_runtime_m_in_its_padding.
+    Built at S == N == 256, the F8_128x4 row-quant scale has rup(S, 128) == 256 rows, which
+    equal the kernel's M: the token count, or the weights' N under swap-AB. A call with fewer
+    tokens in the same 128-row padding runs; under swap-AB it also has fewer weight columns,
+    in the same 4-block padding, which is what moves the kernel's M. GATHER counts S in routed
+    rows (token_index), apart from the token operand's 137 source rows."""
+    E, N, K, bs = 2, 256, 128, 32
+    build_s, call_s, source_rows = 256, 200, 137
+    scale_shape = _quant_scale_shape(build_s, N, True)
+    graph = _build_graph(
+        E, source_rows if gather else build_s, N, K, quant=True, quant_scale_reorder=True, quant_scale_dim=scale_shape, gather_rows=build_s if gather else None
+    )
+    compiled = _plan(graph, config=by_name(_SM120_CFG), swap_ab=swap_ab)
+    assert compiled._compiled.config.swap_ab is swap_ab
+    assert compiled.chain.moe.mode == ("gather" if gather else "none")
+
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    token = torch.randint(-2, 3, (1, source_rows if gather else call_s, K), device="cuda").to(torch.bfloat16)

+    offsets = _offsets([120, call_s - 120], call_s)
+    q = torch.empty(1, call_s, call_n, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
+    q_scale = torch.zeros(*scale_shape, dtype=torch.float8_e8m0fnu, device="cuda")
+    vp = _vp_moe(compiled, token, weight, offsets, [q, q_scale])
+    routed = token
+    if gather:
+        index = torch.randint(source_rows, (1, call_s, 1), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+        vp[compiled.binding.token_index] = index
+        routed = token[:, index.flatten().long()]
+    compiled(vp)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    q_ref, scale_ref = _block_quant_ref(_ref_f32(routed, weight, offsets, call_s, call_n, E), bs, torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(q_scale.float(), _to_blocked(scale_ref[0]).view_as(q_scale).float(), atol=0, rtol=0)

**Codex bot review · model: `gpt-6-astra`**

Reviewed `d6c7d11c1f8a` against base `0f5c79988df0`.

The fake-shape change resolves the demonstrated binding mismatch while the host retains fixed scale-buffer shapes and runtime padding checks. One nonblocking test-gating issue remains: six new cases fail under the default SM100 compiler family instead of skipping.

**[P2] Gate the new SM120 quant-scale tests before selecting the default compiler** ([source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/d6c7d11c1f8a952523cf103dc2c1f142f530a1c5/test/python/gemm/frost/test_matmul.py#L3457))

On native SM100 with the default compiler family, all four new dense cases and both new plain-MoE cases fail with block_scale_quantize's block_size=32, vsize=8 rejection. The SM100 quant validator runs before the family mismatch that the fixture would turn into a skip. These L0 tests therefore add six failures to the SM100 suite. Gate both new test functions for their intended family before calling _plan, or explicitly select the supported SM120 compiler path. The block-scale test already has a requires_sm120 marker.

Evidence: Default-family focused run: 6 failed, 2 skipped. All six failures originate in sm100/compiler.py::_check_block_quant_supported before family mismatch. Same head with SM120 family selected on native SM100: 6 passed, 2 skipped; combined current-base source gives the same result. Attribution: Introduced by the ungated dense and plain-MoE regression tests in this PR.

Validation: Reviewed all four changed files and traced CONST output-shape rules, dense lowered launch checks, MoE output checks and SM120 runtime quantization validation. Fresh fake symbols do not remove those host checks. Six dense/plain-MoE cases passed through the SM120 compiler family on native SM100, including both orientations, row/column quantization and the unaligned-build control. The four dense cases also rejected calls outside their declared scale-padding range. Two native SM120 block-scale cases skipped. Restoring only the base fake-shape emitter reproduced five runtime binding failures; the unaligned-build control passed. The change merges cleanly with the current base. The combined source also passed the six intended-family cases, with two block-scale skips. Requested standard CI with target none; the default SM100 GPU lane would repeat the confirmed test-family failures.

Limitations: No native SM120 or block-scale execution, GATHER validation, graph replay or performance measurement. The SM100 compiler implementation is unchanged and was not qualified for this dynamic-shape fix.

Approved: no P0 or high-risk P1 found. Remaining findings stay with the owner; merge timing stays with the owner.
